Q1: Bis(4-(dimethylamino)phenyl)methanone demonstrates known significant hazards, classified as Tier 1 for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR1), and for dermal and eye hazards (SKN1) based on official GHS criteria. While its endocrine disruption potential is categorized as a demonstrated low/moderate hazard (EDC3) from direct studies, its environmental, inhalation, oral, and organ/systemic hazard profiles are currently considered data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical is listed on several prominent lists of concern, indicating potential risks to human health and the environment. It is included in California's Proposition 65 due to its link to cancer and reproductive harm, and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classifies it as "possibly carcinogenic to humans" (Group 2B). Furthermore, it is featured on the ChemSEC "Substitute It Now" (SIN) List, identifying it as a hazardous chemical for which substitution is recommended.
Q3: This chemical is relatively well-characterized structurally, possessing a defined molecular formula and identified as a 'Small Molecule' rather than an incompletely defined substance or UVCB. With 3,549 literature references, it is significantly more studied than most chemicals in our dataset of fracking and petrochemical materials, indicating substantial scientific attention. Despite this extensive general study, four out of seven hazard categories remain data deficient (Tier 4), suggesting specific hazard assessments for environmental, inhalation, oral, and organ/systemic effects are incomplete.
